title: Kashk-e bademjan
subtitle: Persian aubergine dip with whey, caramelised onion, and walnuts
excerpt: Kashk-e bademjan is a deeply savoury Persian dip made from fried aubergine mixed with kashk (a thick, tangy dried whey), topped with caramelised onion, toasted walnuts, and a drizzle of dried mint in oil. It is rich, complex, and completely unlike anything else on a mezze table.
sourceNotes: A classic Persian dip. Kashk is a preserved whey product common in Persian, Afghan, and Turkish cooking. Strained yoghurt or soured cream are workable substitutes in the UK.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dip keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Add the toppings fresh when serving.

content.text: Kashk-e bademjan sits somewhere between a dip and a spread, and it is extraordinary. Aubergines are fried until caramelised and completely soft, then mashed and mixed with kashk, a thick fermented whey with a sharp, salty tang.

The toppings are what make it dramatic: dark caramelised onions, toasted walnuts, and a swirl of dried mint in hot oil poured over just before serving. The onions give sweetness and body; the walnuts give crunch.

Kashk is sold in Iranian grocery shops and some Middle Eastern food stores, often in jars labelled kashk or whey. Soured cream mixed with a little strained yoghurt is the closest substitute. The flavour will be milder but the texture is right.

Cut the aubergines into 2 cm dice. Heat the olive oil in the large frying pan over medium heat. Add the aubergine, turmeric, and salt. Cook, stirring every few minutes, for 20 to 25 minutes until the aubergine is very soft, golden brown, and has reduced to about half its original volume. Add the garlic for the final 2 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and mash roughly with a fork; it should be chunky rather than a smooth paste.

While the aubergine cooks, heat 3 tbsp olive oil in the small frying pan over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 25 minutes until deeply golden and caramelised. Set aside.

Stir the yoghurt or kashk through the mashed aubergine. Taste and adjust the salt. Spread on a flat plate or into a bowl. Top with the caramelised onions and toasted walnuts. Melt the butter in the small pan over medium heat, add the dried mint, and drizzle immediately over the dip. Add the saffron water if using. Serve at room temperature with flatbread.

rows.cause: Pan overcrowded or heat too low
rows.fix: Fry in batches if needed. The aubergine must be able to colour and dry out, not steam.
Start with less yoghurt and add gradually. Taste as you go.

rows.cause: Heat too high and stirred too often
rows.fix: Keep the heat at medium and stir every 5 minutes only. Rushing caramelised onions always fails.

content.text: For a smoky version, grill or char the whole aubergines over a gas flame before peeling; this gives the finished dip a much deeper, smokier flavour. Kashk-e bademjan can also be served warm rather than at room temperature.
The aubergine and yoghurt base keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Caramelise the onions ahead too. Add the walnut and mint butter topping fresh when serving.

Kashk-e bademjan is a staple mezze of Iranian cooking, served as a starter or part of the spread that accompanies rice and main dishes. It appears in Persian restaurants and homes across Iran and in the diaspora. The combination of aubergine and kashk is ancient and appears in Persian cooking across many centuries.
